name: Xuanzang returns to Chang'an with 657 Buddhist texts
summary: After sixteen years in Central Asia and India, including extended study at Nalanda monastery, Xuanzang returns with 657 Sanskrit manuscripts and Buddha relics. Tang Taizong establishes a translation bureau at the Da Cien temple; over the next two decades Xuanzang and his team translate 76 sutras (~1,300 fascicles) into Chinese.

_quarry.structural_significance: Largest single transmission of Sanskrit Buddhist literature into Chinese; founds the East Asian Yogacara school (Faxiang). His Da Tang Xiyu Ji ('Records of the Western Regions') becomes the principal Chinese-language geography of Central and South Asia and the basis of British archaeological expeditions to Buddhist sites in the 19th–20th centuries.
